measurement_contract_source: explicit provider mapping of measurement_provenance_dictionary.csv, cross-checked against the P0-06 coverage table

notes: the P0-06 coverage table is being rebuilt by a parallel workstream; the sha256 above is of the exact bytes read by this run, and the classes scored here come from the explicit mapping, not from that table
this run's four-class mapping agrees with P0-06's dictionary-derived statistic_class for every provider present in the two panels

P0-06's station-level cross-check column disagrees with the class used here for chmi, foen, gkd_bayern, lubw: that column carries them as undocumented/unverified while the dictionary documents either a daily mean or a project-derived daily mean. This is an internal P0-06 conservatism difference, not a difference in the classes scored here
no station-level cross-check row exists in P0-06 for hubeau, uk_ea, usgs, so that column could not be checked for them

usgs.basis: statistic code 00003 is documented as MEAN VALUES (dictionary)

foen.basis: provider field data_1day_mean, documented daily mean (dictionary)

gkd_bayern.basis: Tageswerte/tmw; CSV column read by the parser is 'Mittelwert' (dictionary)

uk_ea.basis: measure labelled 'Daily mean Temperature (C) time series', valueType mean (dictionary)

chmi.basis: source series TO = instantaneous 10-min; parser averages to a project calendar day (dictionary)

rws_waterwebservices.basis: raw 'meting' values averaged per calendar date; provider GEM24H mean not used (dictionary)

hubeau.basis: continuous chronicle, per-measurement timestamps, resampled to a calendar-day mean (dictionary)

syke.basis: morning ~08:00 near-shore reading, not a provider daily mean (dictionary)

arso.basis: no fetched page states whether the daily value is a mean or a fixed-hour reading (dictionary)

smhi.basis: daily cadence documented, aggregation statistic explicitly unverified (dictionary)

endpoint.contrast_sign: risk minus length; negative = fitted risk score has the lower failure rate

retention_helper_exact_vs_step2_grid.note: Step 2 searches RETENTION_GRID then a 0.01 grid; the exact helper takes any k, so it can only be equal or finer.

sources_checked.what_it_is: labelled daily panel with high_temperature and heatwave_min_3d columns
sources_checked.why_not: station ids are the anonymised GEMS benchmark ids, not river-temperature station ids, and the labelled variables are air temperature T and flow F; it cannot label a station-year of the WRR panel

sources_checked.what_it_is: gap-segment diagnostic with a derived 'heatwave_fraction' column (share of gap days above the station's training 90th percentile of daily temperature)
sources_checked.belongs_to_this_panel: different unit of analysis (gap segments, not station-years)
sources_checked.why_not: it is a derived warm-day overlap computed by the project, not a provider or third-party event label, and it does not identify heatwave episodes

event_label_audit.conclusion: No true heatwave/event label exists for the river-temperature panel. The only labelled event file in the repository is the anonymised GEMS benchmark panel. The thermal strata below are therefore warm-year strata and must not be read as an event-scale heatwave analysis.

known_limitations: the case table's reconstructor features were built under fit_protocol=leave_one_year_out, so the time-transfer rows are honest for the risk score's training block but remain an upper bound on a strictly prior-years deployment
wave-2 rows are exploratory and do not retune or replace the wave-2 seal, which belongs to the frozen multi-method certificate screen
no true heatwave event labels exist for this panel, so thermal strata are warm-year strata
threshold-transfer intervals resample networks inside the calibration block as well as the evaluation block, so they carry threshold uncertainty as well as evaluation uncertainty
